recipes.name: Make-Ahead Vegetarian Moroccan Stew
ingredients_raw: 2 medium sweet potatoes, peeled and diced
1 teaspoon ground black pepper, to taste

steps.text: Make the spice mixture: Mix cinnamon, cumin, salt, ginger, cloves, nutmeg, turmeric, and curry powder together in a bowl.

Make the stew: Melt butter in a large pot over medium heat. Add onion and cook until soft and just beginning to brown, 5 to 10 minutes. Stir in kale and spice mixture; cook and stir until kale begins to wilt and spices are fragrant, about 2 minutes.
Add broth, garbanzo beans, tomatoes, potatoes, sweet potatoes, carrots, lentils, apricots, and honey; stir to combine and bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat to low and simmer for 5 minutes. Remove from the heat and let cool for 30 to 40 minutes. Cover the pot and refrigerate for up to 3 days.

When ready to eat, remove from the refrigerator and bring to a boil. Reduce the heat and simmer until vegetables are tender and stew is heated through, about 25 minutes. Season with black pepper. If a thicker stew is desired, dissolve cornstarch in water. Stir mixture into stew and simmer until thickened, about 5 more minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Make-Ahead Vegetarian Moroccan Stew
raw_recipe.description: This Moroccan stew may have a long list of ingredients, but don't let it scare you. It comes together very easily for a rich and flavorful meal.

review.reviewBody: For the love of all that is holy DO NOT DOUBLE THIS RECIPE. I did, thinking it would feed our three person family for three days like that, instead it turned into one of the most absurd kitchen experiences I have ever had, with both my husband and I sous cheffing for hours in the midst of crying babies and toddlers, and ultimately all three of our giant pots so that they couldn't even all fit on the stove simultaneously while it simmered, etc. THIS MAKES A TON OF FOOD AS IS. Unless you are feeding hundred or thousands or hundreds of thousands of people, DO NOT DOUBLE THIS.

Yes made changes! Crowd pleaser! Here are my recipe alterations. Used the big oval Crock-Pot and with three 32oz cartons of organic chicken stock, we needed it! Skip the apricots, substituted raisins. Used 5 large carrots. Skipped the honey, substituted 3 TBS of maple syrup. Doubled the initial spice mixture that is cooked with the onion and kale at the beginning of the recipe. Used 3-4 cups of kale. I de-veined the tougher leaves and finely chopped then stirred directly into the broth. Skipped the cloves. Substituted the white potatoes for the firmer chopped butternut squash, (about 4 cups). Added a total of two sweet potatoes. Added one more chopped onion. Used only the 1 (14.5 ounce) can of diced tomatoes. Hold adding lentils and garbanzo beans until serving day. Cook lentils separately. Right before serving the stew, I added in the red lentils (with a generous amount of extra stew spices), and stirred the stew. Though I overcooked (boiled over) the red lentils, they were a blessing as stew thickener and in my opinion a surprise key to this stew’s success. Before final reheat add garbanzo beans to maintain bean firmness, and 1TBS dried red pepper to add zip. I did move the stew into three large saucepans to get bubbly all at same time. Stirred often. Pass around the dining table a big bowl of 2% fat Greek yogurt and fresh cilantro to finish. Served stew with crispy chunky bread on the side. Revisions to original recipe are compilations of many reviewer’s ideas noted in this stew recipe’s reviews. My revised amounts completely filled the large oval Crock-Pot, and served 13 people. Everyone asked for the recipe!

So delicious, closest thing I've ever found to my favorite Nile Spice Couscous Lentil Curry soup, and will definitely make again (would be delicious served with couscous). I made the following adjustments: (1) Doubled the amount of curry powder; (2) Added a few cloves of minced garlic when I added the dry spices; (3) Reduced amount of potato - used 2 russet potatoes, 1 sweet potato and a cup of chopped zucchini (add the zucchini towards the end of cooking so that it doesn't get too mushy); (4) Reduced the amount of apricots [used 4 small apricots]; (5) Didn't add honey; and (6) skipped the optional cornstarch. An instant favorite.

I love this dish! It's hearty, filling, and goes over well with my vegetarian friends. You can easily make this a vegan dish by using coconut oil instead of butter, and maple syrup instead of honey.

For my dish, I added turnip, parsnip, and extra kale. I substituted the honey for maple syrup, and I added a couple chopped dried mango slices, and half the apricots. 

The next time I make it, I'll be adding some garlic to the onions while they sauté, for some additional flavour. 

This dish makes a ton of food! Serve it with crusty bread and enjoy!

Made it twice and the only change was the second time I left out the honey, which then made it completely Vegan. It was a great blend of seasonings.The sweet potato and dried apricot added a great sweetness to the stew. It was better the next day also. I had some left overs so I ladled them into freezer bags. Each with enough for two servings and froze them. Have pulled them out for a couples of lunches since, defrosted them in the refrigerator overnight , heated in microwave till hot, added a piece of 21 grain bread and just as yummy as when it was first made. 
Now on my, regular staple list, and have given the recipe to my daughter, and step-son (he is vegan). 
Thank you for this great recipe.

This is so good and healthy. One of those recipes we crave because it is delicious and makes the body feel good. I add a can of sweet peas. I also always make the corn starch slurry and add it. The thickened broth is just so satisfyingly more stew-like. This makes a lot. As one reviewer noted it would be a very bad idea to double this. I am a chronic recipe doubler and I would never make two batches of this at once because it fills my largest soup kettle to the top.

Skipped lentils and actual sweet potato (used 1-1/2 cups of leftover mashed sweet potatoes from Thanksgiving).I only used 30-40 oz of broth and at least doubled the indicated spice amounts. But that combo of spices makes this taste a little sweet once the tomatoes cook down. Additional salt and 2 tablespoons of Apple cider vinegar (or any vinegar or acid like lemon juice) really helped balance out the sweetness and make it balanced again.Only took about 30 mins of boiling to bring it all together for first day servings (which tasted great).

Flavors are great, in my opinion the cooking procedure ruins this. The vegetables and lentils have significantly different cooking times and the vegetables in this turn to mush. In addition there is no reason to add the kale until the end. This recipe makes a lot and unfortunately just didn’t want to eat more of it due to unappetizing textures and appearance. I rarely leave poor reviews but this calls for ingredients that aren’t just lying around and is also a fair amount of prep work. Recommend cooking the lentils separately, checking the vegetables after ~5 mins of cooking depending on size, and adding the kale toward the very end.

PROS:
1. Excellent flavor and spice palate!
2. Makes a TON of food.
3. Great freezer meal, just chop and freeze all the veggies.
4. Filling way to go meatless if your family isn't quite on board.
CONS:
1. The recipe calls for way too many potatoes and sweet potatoes - I recommend halving the amounts if you want everything to fit in a large pot - otherwise you should use an actual stock pot. 
2. If you add even 2/3 of the recommended root veggies, there's not enough broth to cover them. Again, less root veg OR bigger pot and more broth.
3. It does need a kick to liven it up, curry is good.
CHANGES:
1. I didn't have apricots so I used raisins and it tasted fine.
2. I used homemade chicken stock instead of veggie broth.
3. Wait to add the garbanzo beans until five minutes before the rest of the stew is done, otherwise they turn to mush.

Made this in the slow cooker after looking for tips. Other sources recommended using onion powder and garlic powder instead of raw, or otherwise pre-sauteeing the onion & garlic before starting the slow cook. For our house, it could have been a bit spicier, so I would add red pepper next time, but the combination of fragrant spices was lovely. Lentil, chickpea and 2 potatoe types makes this a well-balanced meal nutrition-wise for vegetarians!

I made some tweaks to make the recipe vegan and it was delicious! Even more flavorful on day 2! Excluded butter and sautéed in olive oil. Also, Instead of broth I used water & 2 tbsp Tom paste. I added corn (to entice my son) and used red kidney beans instead of lentils; added chili powder and instead of the regular potatoes, I added jack fruit for some sweetness (I did still include sweet potatoes which were yummy)! Absolutely delicious!!!! Thanks for giving me the base ingredients for your wonderful, healthy stew!! This will become a staple!!

Wonderful, soul warming stew. I did not have lentils, but otherwise followed the recipe. A bit of prep but well worth it. It makes a lot of stew!! My friends loved it! Glad to have the freezing instructions included. Thank you for this recipe.
I made the recipe just as stated above and may I say that it's a very delicious dish with mildly interested flavors. I am going to be making this again 😁
Maybe add less cinnamon and cook carrots longer next time

As a vegetarian I like something healthy and hearty. This recipe most definitely is one of my favorites. I made it in an instant pot and it was quick and well worth taking the time and cutting up the vegetables. I used spinach instead of kale, only sweet potatoes, next time I want to double up on the chickpeas, I used more vegetable broth and crushed tomatos instead of pieces of tomato. Yummy!!! The flavor is superb. I did nothing to those dry ingredients. 👍⭐

Followed the recipe concerning the amounts and types of spices. Used chicken stock instead of vegetable stock and substituted collard greens for the kale (since that's what I had), also didn't add the apricots because I didn't have any. I made quinoa for the suggested side and added crushed caraway to that. When I served it, I added a dollop of greek yogurt on top with cilantro. It was all really delish!
Very tasty! I had more sweet potato than reg potatoes, used less of them overall as well as 3 carrots. Still very bountiful recipe.
My first time making it and love it with all the veggies in it. I added a little more curry to overcome the taste of cloves.
Delicious with good bread and butter. Made a ton!!!

I had this about 7 years ago for the first time when a college friend made it. Randomly, I started craving it and this recipe did not disappoint. This is definitely one of my staple meals. Comforting and exciting! Make it for yourself, family, dinner with friends, etc. I paired it with some basmati rice, homemade tzatziki sauce, and butter naan. So delish! ;)
